title: ComfortVent-CO2Pilot: Comparing Optimal Modes For Non-Invasive Ventilation In High CO2 - a Pilot Randomized Crossover Study
summary:
Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is a good alternative to invasive ventilation because it causes less damage to the lungs. However, it is not yet clear which type of ventilation is best. A new ventilation mode is called bilevel NRV. It does not support breathing in a synchronized manner, but provides an evenly increasing and decreasing pressure. The study investigates which ventilation mode patients with hypercapnia find better: mandatory BiLevel or BiLevel NRV. Patients rate their comfort on a scale from 0 to 10.
After giving written consent, patients are randomly assigned one of the two ventilation modes. This ventilation lasts a maximum of 2 hours and is monitored using a device to measure lung resistance. Patients then take a break for at least 15 minutes. They then test the other ventilation mode.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients in intensive care units/ICU wards with hypercapnia (PaCO2 or PkapCO2 >45 mmHg) and clinical indication for non-invasive ventilation
- Age over 18 years
- Consent to study participation by the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- GCS < 14
- Lack of ability to give consent or communicate
- Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) according to Berlin definition
- Pulmonary fibrosis
- Contraindications for non-invasive ventilation, such as facial injuries, upper airway obstructions, lack of protective reflexes, recurrent vomiting, ileus, allergies to mask or EIT belt components
- PaO2/FiO2 ratio ≤ 100 mmHg or SpO2/FiO2 ratio ≤ 148 (with SpO2 ≤ 97%)
- Neither arterial access nor valid SpO2 measurement available
- Thoracic injuries: unrelieved pneumothorax, open wounds of the thorax
None of the above exclusion criteria may be met if a patient is to be included in the study.
